MANURES.
The quantity, quality, and proper application of ma-
nures is of the utmost importance in all gardening opera-

the heavy crops

Of
stable or barn-yard manure, from

for at least six months jireviously, by thoroughly turning

heating unduly.
The
usual method
is to have the manure yard formed in a
low part of the garden, but if there is no natural depres-
sion, one may be made by digging. out an area
fifty by
one hundred feet and from eighteen to twenty-four inches
deep, and enclosing it by a fence about six feet in height.
The wagons are driven alongside, and

to have

spread regularly
